questions.q: Where does Sadhguru say happiness must be found?
a: Within, by generating the right internal state
In a career that matches your talents
In the approval of the people around you
In a simple life close to nature
questions.why: Lesson 1 says fixation on outer circumstances prevents fulfillment; perceptions happen within us.

questions.q: What does response-ability mean to Sadhguru?
a: Responding consciously rather than reacting on impulse
Carrying more duties than others expect of you
Accepting blame when a situation goes wrong
Keeping your emotions hidden in a crisis
questions.why: Lesson 2 defines it as the capacity to answer life with awareness instead of unconscious reactions.

questions.q: Why does Sadhguru connect more responsibility with more freedom?
a: Awareness reveals options, so you can choose your response
Obligations force you to become more disciplined
Freedom only comes after you meet every duty
Others trust you more when you take charge
questions.why: Lesson 2 says growing awareness shows you the choices available in any situation.

questions.q: What does the story of Heraclitus digging with a spoon illustrate?
a: The mind is too small to hold the whole truth
Persistence matters more than raw intelligence
Philosophers often waste time on useless tasks
Small tools can accomplish surprising things
questions.why: Lesson 3 uses the anecdote to urge humility about how much the intellect can know.

questions.q: What role do the asanas play in the original yogic tradition?
a: One of eight branches of a larger system
The only practice needed for inner growth
A warm-up before meditation begins
A cure for most physical illnesses
questions.why: The overview says physical postures are just one of eight branches of yogic knowledge.
